Solutions 1 and 2 give N, and Solution 3 gives N(N−1)/2. None of these matches what I recall for this hierarchy, which is N(N+1)/2. I am not certain of that recollection, so treat this as a judgment rather than a verified result.

The N = 1 case is the most reliable check. The single algebraic soliton has a denominator quadratic in x with complex-conjugate roots, so it has exactly one pole in the upper half-plane. Solution 3 gives 0 at N = 1, which is wrong. Solutions 1 and 2 give 1 there, which fits, but their formula N does not match the triangular count N(N+1)/2, which equals 1, 3, 6, … for N = 1, 2, 3. The tau-function degree in the double-Wronskian construction is consistent with that triangular growth. Since the answer I recall differs from all three, none of the proposed solutions is correct.

CHOICE: NONE
